page.layout: Running head with page number at top left, above the text. Below it, two round portraits side by side (left: Picus, right: Agricola), each with a legend around the rim. Below them one text column of two paragraphs. No margin notes, no bottom matter.

main_text.p: PICVS Mirandula Phœnix appellabatur, quòd in eum Dij superi supra familiæ claritatem omnis corporis, ac animi vel rarissima dona contulerint. Decorus fuit, moribus lectissi-mis, incomparabili facundia, qua omnes eius seculi sapientes in admirationem sui facilè conuertit. Astrologos infectatus est eo grauissimo opere, nec dum absoluto quo totius diuinationis vanitatem confutauit. Scripsit doctissimè de re Theologica, & Philosophia: huiusque opera sunt impressa Basileæ, vno volumine. Excessit è vita, trium & triginta annorum iuuenis, eo die quo Carolus Galliæ Rex Octauus, Napolim est ingressus, anno salutis 1483. Nepotem habuit Franciscum Picum Mirandulam, virum doctissimum, qui interfectus fuit cum Alberto filio, à Galeotto fratris filio.

GEORGIVS Agricola, insignis Medicus, propter eius magnam diuersamque eruditionem, dignus est adprimè qui eorum catalogo ascribatur, quorum memoria monumentis scriptisque est percelebris: quàm vt magis decoremus, eius figurâ nō noluimus hîc inserere. Conscripsit quinque libros, de pōderibus & mēsuris quinque alios, de pōderibus & mēsuris Romanorū & Græcorū: duos, de pōderibus & mēsuris exterarū nationum: tres, de pretio metallorum & monetarum: vnum, de animalibus subterraneis: duodecim, de re[?] metallica, in quibus ad amussim expressæ sunt imagines officiorū, instrumentorum, machinarum, omniumque aliarum rerum, quæ ad rem metallicam pertinent, lectu & memoria dignissimæ.

page.notes: Two woodcut medallions with printed legends around the rims. Left medallion: a profile bust in a cap, legend in the upper arc reads roughly "PICVS" with the lower arc "MIRANDVLA" and "D·C·C·C·D" type marks; partly illegible, not transcribed. Right medallion: a bust of an older man in a hat, legend "GEORG." on the left and "AGRICOLA" on the right. Doubtful readings: "mēsuris" and "pōderibus" (macrons/abbreviation marks may be ligatures of the printed text); "de re[?] metallica" (the letter after "de" is damaged in the scan); "fui" in the first paragraph is read as "sui" (long s). Page number is printed as "212" (old-style figures in the scan).
